# Radoslav Radev Recommends Having A Strategy And Structure For Planche Progression Timing

Radoslav Radev recommends having a strategy and structure for planche training to avoid going too early or too late to the next progression, and says the current progression will not teach you on the next one. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 04:03]

## Details

- He says the third thing is really important: to have strategy and structure, because without a strategy a lot of people lose time by going too early on the next progression without enough foundation on the current one. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 04:03]
- Going too early on the next progression loses protraction, builds wrong habits with wrong technique, and ends up with bad form. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 04:17]
- He says the current progression will not teach you on the next one: the straddle planche will not teach you on full planche, the tuck planche will not teach you on advanced tuck, and the advanced tuck will not teach you on the straddle planche. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 04:55]
- Staying too much time on the current progression is also bad and you will lose time. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 05:04]
- People who stay too long get angry, it hits them in the ego, and they start training more and more, tiring their nervous system because they train every day trying to hold the progression more. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 05:10]
- He says they exhaust their nervous system and lose progress, going from 15 seconds record on advanced planche to 10 or 8 or 5 seconds. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 05:25]
- Having a structure and strategy for how many seconds to hold, when to go to the next progression, how to go to the next progressions, what are the progressions between the progressions, and how long to be on the exact current progression helps you not lose time by going too early or too late. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 05:45]
- The strategy and structure for the week helps you be consistent and to track your results and to think when is the best time to go on the next progression. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 06:07]
- Without a strategy, people just do the tuck planche, see how long the journey is to full planche, think it is not for them, go back to weighted pull-ups and dips, and after five years still do not have the planche. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 06:29]
- Following a strategy makes you consistent. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 06:40]

## Evidence

- vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 04:03 (Radoslav Radev): "the third thing guys is really really important to have strategy and structure because if you don't have a strategy a lot of people losing a lot of time because they're going too early on the next progression"
- vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 04:13 (Radoslav Radev): "they don't have enough foundation on the current progression they don't do the right technique the right activation and they're going to the next progression too early and they losing protraction building wrong habits with the wrong technique ends up with bad form"
- vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 04:55 (Radoslav Radev): "the straddle planche will not teach me on full planche the tuck planche will not teach you on advanced tuck the advanced tuck will not teach you on the straddle planche so if you stay too much time on the current progression that's bad and you will lose time"
- vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 05:10 (Radoslav Radev): "most of the people in this situation they getting angry it hitting them in the ego and they start training more and more and more and more the advanced tuck planche for example and they tired their nervous system because they train every day"
- vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 05:25 (Radoslav Radev): "they losing progress from 15 seconds record on advanced planche they're going to 10 or 8 or 5 seconds because they exhausting their nervous system"
- vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 05:45 (Radoslav Radev): "if you have a structure and strategy for the future how many seconds i will hold this or that when to go on the next progression how to go on the next progressions what are the progressions between the progressions"
- vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 05:55 (Radoslav Radev): "and how long to be on the exact current progression is will help you a lot to not losing time to go too early on the next progression or too late"
- vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 06:07 (Radoslav Radev): "the strategy and the structure for the week helping you to be consistent"
- vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 06:45 (Radoslav Radev): "you can train three times per week but consistent and to track your results and to think when and how is the best time the best time to go on the next progression"
- vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 06:18 (Radoslav Radev): "a lot of people want to achieve the planche they trying planche hold tuck planche they don't have any strategy they just doing the tuck planche and they see how long journey is from took [tuck] planche to full planche and they're like well that's not for me"
- vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 06:29 (Radoslav Radev): "they're going back to the weighted pull-ups and dips and after five years they still don't have the the planche"
- vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 06:40 (Radoslav Radev): "it's really important to have a strategy and to follow this strategy because it's making you consistent"
